Hello New Home: Local Partner Programme

Prospectus for mentees (read this before you apply)

Version 0.1, draft for founder sign-off, 16 October 2026.

This document is not legal, tax or financial advice. It describes a programme that Hello New Home intends to run. The money figures are illustrations built on fees that are still marked [CONFIRM] (they have not yet been signed off and may change before launch). Anything marked [VERIFY] is a point we have checked against public sources but have not yet had confirmed in writing by the regulator or a solicitor. The partner agreement itself will be drafted by a solicitor; nothing here creates a contract. Take your own advice on tax and employment status before you sign anything.

1. Why this exists

Hello New Home is a Rent Smart Wales licensed letting agent in Swansea. It already manages single lets and HMOs (through hellomyroom), and is adding serviced accommodation (SA) management in 2026.

Most mentees who want property income without buying stock hit the same wall: "I'll start a letting agency" turns, within a fortnight, into Rent Smart Wales agent licensing, client money protection, professional indemnity insurance, a redress scheme, a CRM, portal subscriptions, referencing contracts, deposit scheme accounts and a compliance calendar. That is a £10–20k, 6–12 month build before the first landlord says yes, and it is the reason most people never start.

The Local Partner programme splits the job in two:

  • You do the part that only a local person can do: being known in your patch, finding landlords and short-let owners, meeting them, and (as an Area Partner) doing the viewings, inspections and check-ins on the ground.
  • HQ in Swansea does everything regulated: contracts, referencing, deposits, client money, rent collection, compliance, maintenance, statements, complaints.

You earn a share of the management fee on every property you bring in, for as long as it stays managed. You never handle money, never sign a contract, and never need your own agent licence or insurance stack to start.

This is not a franchise. There is no buy-in for the founding cohort. It is a licensed introducer / area partner arrangement, papered by a solicitor, where territories are earned rather than sold.

3. The two tiers

Introducer

  • Who: any current mentee in good standing.
  • What you do: find landlords and SA owners, have the first conversation, book them a Free Rent Review or SA Income Appraisal with HQ, and hand over. HQ does everything after the introduction.
  • What you earn: 25% of HNH's net management fee [CONFIRM] on every instruction you introduce, for as long as HNH manages it, plus £100 [CONFIRM] for each SA unit that goes live.
  • What it costs: nothing. No fee, no minimum.
  • What you must not do: any "lettings work" or "property management work" in the Rent Smart Wales sense. No viewings, no inspections, no inventories, no collecting rent, no being the tenant's point of contact. Introducers introduce; that is the whole job. (See section 7 on why.)

Area Partner

  • Who: Introducers who have brought in 3 or more instructions, completed the requirements in section 7, and been interviewed by the founder.
  • What you do: everything an Introducer does, plus: an exclusive postcode territory; viewings, property inspections, check-ins and check-outs in that territory for HNH-managed properties; local networking; your area page and local social presence.
  • What you earn: 50% of net management fee [CONFIRM] on your own instructions; 25% [CONFIRM] on HQ-originated instructions in your territory that you service; the SA go-live payment as above.
  • What it costs: £0 upfront for the founding cohort; £99 per month systems and brand fee from month 4 [CONFIRM]. Your own car, phone, mileage and any local marketing beyond the HQ-supplied templates.

Both tiers are self-employed. You invoice (or are self-billed by) HNH and you are responsible for your own tax and National Insurance. HNH will not deduct PAYE. Take advice on your employment status; the agreement will be drafted as a contract for services, not employment [VERIFY with accountant/solicitor].

4. How the money flows

What "net management fee" means (plain version; the agreement will carry the legal definition): the recurring monthly management fee HNH actually receives from the landlord or owner for that property, after any discount, refund or fee-free period, and excluding one-off fees (setup, Tenant Find, SA Launch), pass-through costs (cleaning, repairs, linen), third-party product premiums (rent guarantee) and anything HNH has to refund. Whether the base is stated inclusive or exclusive of VAT is a [CONFIRM] decision; the examples below follow the offer architecture and use the fee with any VAT shown where it applies (HNH is not VAT-registered, so none is added); VAT, so if HQ settles on an ex-VAT base, divide each commission figure by 1.2.

Timing: commission is earned when HNH receives the fee, not when the landlord signs. It is paid monthly in arrears on a statement HQ issues. If a landlord is on the 3-months-free switch offer, there is no fee for those months and therefore no commission for those months. If HNH refunds a fee (for example under the SA 90-day guarantee), the matching commission is clawed back from your next statement.

The published fee sheet is the only price list. Current headline fees (all [CONFIRM]):

Notes on all three:

  • The fee cap works against you on high rents. At £1,400 rent the fee is capped at £150, so an Area Partner's 50% is £75, not £84. On the typical Swansea rent the cap does not bite.
  • Managed+ (Full Management + £25/month) pays slightly more per unit; the examples assume everyone is on standard Full Management.
  • Landlords sell, move back in or leave. Expect to lose roughly 10% of units a year [VERIFY against HNH's own churn] and plan to replace them.
  • Getting from 0 to 30 units at 2–4 instructions a month takes 12–18 months of steady work. Nobody in cohort one has done it yet; these figures are modelled, not observed.

5. What a partner actually does, week to week

Introducer (3–6 hours a week):

  • Keep a list of every landlord and short-let owner you know or meet. Add 5–10 a week.
  • Have conversations: at your mentoring group, at local networking, with people who mention "my flat in Swansea".
  • Book Free Rent Reviews and SA Income Appraisals through your tracked link. HQ calls within one working day.
  • Log every lead in the CRM the same day. If it is not in the CRM, it is not yours.

Area Partner (15–25 hours a week, more as the portfolio grows):

WhenWhat
MondayPipeline review with HQ (15 minutes); plan the week's viewings and inspections; GBP post
Tuesday–ThursdayViewings for HNH-listed properties in your territory (daytime and two early evenings); property inspections (quarterly cycle); check-ins and check-outs with photo inventories; one board-canvassing or letter-drop session; one block of landlord calls
FridayAdmin: inspection reports uploaded, CRM updated, next week's appointments confirmed; Facebook group post
WeeklyOne networking event (breakfast club, BNI-type, landlord meetup, chamber, community group); 2–3 Airbnb/short-let host approaches
MonthlyPartner call with HQ; review KPIs; territory review (instructions won, lost, in pipeline)
AlwaysAnswer HQ within 2 working hours on anything tenant-facing; keep inspection SLAs (first inspection within 6 weeks of move-in, then quarterly [CONFIRM])

What you never do, at either tier: take money (including cash, holding deposits or bank transfers), sign anything on HNH's behalf, write or agree tenancy terms, decide referencing outcomes, promise a rent figure that HQ has not confirmed, give legal advice, or quote outside the fee sheet.

7. Rent Smart Wales and the rules you work under

This is the part most "start an agency" plans get wrong, so here it is in plain terms. [VERIFY: all points below checked against Rent Smart Wales guidance and the Housing (Wales) Act 2014 explanatory notes in October 2026; written confirmation from Rent Smart Wales on the partner model is a launch gate.]

  • In Wales, anyone who does lettings work or property management work on behalf of a landlord must hold a Rent Smart Wales agent licence (Housing (Wales) Act 2014, Part 1). Lettings work includes conducting viewings and preparing inventories; property management work includes collecting rent, being the tenant's main point of contact, arranging repairs or access, checking the condition of the property (inspections) and serving notices. Appointing an unlicensed agent exposes the landlord, and acting as one is an offence.
  • A narrow set of things can be done without a licence: publishing adverts and passing on information, provided you do no other lettings work and no property management work at all. That is the box an Introducer stays inside.
  • Hello New Home holds the agent licence. Licensed agents must ensure that their people who carry out lettings or management work complete Rent Smart Wales approved training; the licence is renewed every five years and renewal asks for evidence of that training. Rent Smart Wales guidance is written around "employees" (one industry guide quotes a 12-week window from starting work for new staff to complete training [VERIFY]). Whether a self-employed partner doing viewings and inspections under HNH's licence is treated as HNH's trained staff, or must hold their own agent licence, is the open question. Until Rent Smart Wales confirms in writing, HNH will run the conservative version: every Area Partner completes the approved training before any fieldwork, and the agreement makes you subject to the Rent Smart Wales Code of Practice as if you were HNH staff.
  • Licence conditions on HNH ("Business Safeguards") require client money protection, professional indemnity insurance and membership of a redress scheme (The Property Ombudsman or the Property Redress Scheme). These are HQ's; you rely on them and must never suggest you hold them yourself.
  • Fee transparency. Consumer Rights Act 2015 s.83 requires a letting agent to publish a full list of fees (each described so the payer knows what it covers, with any VAT shown where it applies (HNH is not VAT-registered, so none is added); VAT) at its premises and on its website, plus its client money protection scheme and redress scheme. That is why partners quote only from the published fee sheet: an off-sheet quote is a breach for HNH, with penalties up to £5,000 per breach.
  • England. HNH's licence is a Wales licence. In England there is no agent licence, but letting agents must belong to a redress scheme (since 2014) and, if they hold client money, a client money protection scheme (since 1 April 2019; penalties up to £30,000). The Renters' Rights Act 2025 is being phased in from 2026 with a landlord database and a new ombudsman [VERIFY current phase dates]. Cohort one works in Wales only. Do not take an English instruction unless HQ has told you in writing that it has the English compliance stack in place.
  • Anti-money-laundering. HMRC supervision applies to estate agency (sales) businesses and to letting agency work only where an individual property's rent is €10,000 a month or more (in force since January 2020, per property) [VERIFY current GOV.UK guidance]. Ordinary Swansea lettings fall below that, so HNH is not currently HMRC-supervised for lettings; if HNH ever takes on a let at that level or starts selling property, HQ handles registration. You never take ID documents or payments "to save time".
  • Calling, messaging and letters. Unsolicited marketing calls to numbers on the Telephone Preference Service are unlawful; HQ will screen call lists before you dial [VERIFY TPS screening set-up], and you stop calling anyone who asks. Unsolicited marketing messages (SMS, WhatsApp, email) to individuals need consent, so the message templates in this pack are written as replies to people who have posted or contacted us first. Letters to "The Owner" at an address are fine and carry an opt-out line. Airbnb's terms restrict soliciting hosts through its platform [VERIFY], so host outreach happens in person, through host communities and through hosts' own direct-booking sites, not via Airbnb messaging.
  • Short lets in Wales. Short-letting is lawful but increasingly regulated: a visitor-accommodation register run by the Welsh Revenue Authority starts from autumn 2026, a visitor levy may follow from 2027 at councils' discretion, a licensing scheme under the 2026 Act is due by March 2030, the 182-day / 252-day business-rates rule has applied since April 2023 and is under review, and the C6 short-let planning use class exists so councils can require planning permission in some areas [VERIFY each; the planning point was not confirmed in this pass]. HQ runs the legality check in every SA Income Appraisal. You never tell an owner their unit "is fine".

8. Territory rules (Area Partners)

  • A territory is one or more full postcode districts (for example SA4, or SA6 and SA7 together). HQ keeps its home districts [CONFIRM which: likely SA1–SA3]; everything else in the SA postcode area and, later, neighbouring areas is available.
  • Territories are exclusive for Area Partners: HQ routes web and phone leads from that district to you, and no other Area Partner markets there. Introducers have no territory and may introduce anywhere HNH operates; if an Introducer brings in a property inside your territory, the Introducer gets 25% and you get 25% for servicing it (the same total as your own instruction) [CONFIRM].
  • Exclusivity is kept by performance: at least 2 new instructions per quarter [CONFIRM] after the first six months, inspection and viewing SLAs met, no upheld complaints. Miss two consecutive quarters and HQ may open the district to a second partner or withdraw it; your existing commissions are unaffected.
  • A territory is not property. It cannot be sold, sublet, shared or passed on. If you leave, it returns to HQ.
  • Marketing: you may market only inside your territory (and generally online for your area page). Mentoring-group introductions are the exception and count as Introducer activity wherever the property is.

9. From Introducer to Area Partner

  1. Introduce 3 instructions that go live (any mix of Full Management, Managed+, HMO or SA Management; Tenant Find alone does not count) [CONFIRM].
  2. Pass the 3-month proving period as an Introducer with every lead logged and no conduct issues.
  3. Ask for a territory. HQ checks it is available and that you meet section 6.
  4. Interview with the founder; agree the territory and a 90-day plan (the 30-Day Launch Playbook is the first third of it).
  5. Complete Rent Smart Wales approved training, DBS, car insurance, shadowing.
  6. Sign the Area Partner schedule to the agreement. Your 50% rate applies to instructions signed after that date; earlier introductions stay at 25% [CONFIRM].
  7. Three-month proving period as an Area Partner, then the £99/month fee begins in month 4.

There is no fast track and no fee to skip a step.

10. How it ends

  • Notice. Either side can end the agreement on 30 days' written notice at any time; no reason needed, no exit fee. During the first 3 months of either tier, either side can walk immediately.
  • For cause. HQ can end it immediately for: handling money, signing or promising anything on HNH's behalf, quoting off the fee sheet, misleading a landlord or tenant, discrimination, failure to complete required training, a failed DBS or an undisclosed matter that makes you not fit and proper, breaching data protection, or bringing the brand into disrepute.
  • What happens to commissions (proposal; [CONFIRM] and subject to the solicitor's drafting):
  • Introducer commissions on instructions you introduced continue for as long as HNH manages those properties, provided the agreement ended without cause.
  • Area Partner 50% rates drop to the 25% Introducer rate on your own instructions when you stop servicing them; the 25% servicing share on HQ leads stops when servicing stops.
  • Termination for cause ends all future commissions from the termination date.
  • If you stop being a mentee, no new introductions are accepted; existing commissions continue.
  • Hand-back. You return keys, ID letter, business cards and any HNH materials, delete HNH data from personal devices, and stop using the name. You remain bound by confidentiality and by a 12-month non-solicitation of HNH's landlords, owners, tenants, staff and other partners [CONFIRM period; enforceability is for the solicitor].
  • Brand. The licence to use the Hello New Home name ends the day the agreement does.

11. Honest limits

  • Nobody has yet earned the figures in section 4 under this programme. It is cohort one.
  • Area Partner income depends on the local market, on HQ's conversion of your appraisals and on your own activity. HQ will share conversion data monthly so you can see what is working.
  • The regulatory position for self-employed people doing viewings and inspections under a licensed agent's training rules is the single biggest open item. If Rent Smart Wales says each Area Partner needs their own agent licence, the Area Partner tier will be redesigned (likely as part-time employment or a different scope) before anyone starts fieldwork.
  • This document will be replaced by the signed agreement and the published fee sheet. Where they differ, they win.
